column1: biomass_autocorrelation_decay
column2: Decay rate of the spatial biomass autocorrelation
column3: Change in correlation length of the occupancy field per MCS
column4: Correlation length of the segmented biomass field over time
column12: SELECTED 2026-08-14. Field-level on BOTH sides, so it needs no cell-to-parcel mapping — which is what disqualified single-cell MSD. structure.correlation_length already computes the model side. Selecting now rather than after spatial calibration is deliberate: it makes TIME-RESOLVED stacks a requirement of the campaign, avoiding a static campaign that would have to be repeated. CORRECTION 2026-08-15: the selection commit (2dbc154) also wrote a DIFFERENT statistic into this note — a temporal autocorrelation C_B(dt) = <dB(x,t) dB(x,t+dt)> / <dB(x,t)^2> — while description, model_quantity and experimental_quantity were left byte-identical, still declaring the spatial correlation length tracked across frames. The V. cholerae pilot then implemented the note rather than the declaration. A free-text field cannot amend a declaration. The declared quantity here is unchanged; C_B(dt) is now its own candidate, biomass_temporal_autocorrelation_decay, and is not selected.

column1: biomass_temporal_autocorrelation_decay
column2: Decay of the temporal autocorrelation of the biomass field
column3: Temporal autocorrelation of the occupancy field between MCS separated by dt
column4: Temporal autocorrelation of the segmented biomass field between frames separated by dt
column12: SEPARATED OUT 2026-08-15. This never had a declaration: it entered the ledger on 2026-08-14 as a formula inside biomass_autocorrelation_decay's notes, and the V. cholerae pilot implemented it as though it were the selected observable. It is a legitimate candidate and is recorded as one. C_B(dt) = <dB(x,t) dB(x,t+dt)> / <dB(x,t)^2>, normalised by C(0) computed over the same set of pairs — dividing instead by the variance at t=0 alone lets C(0) exceed 1 whenever the field's variance grows, which is what a developing biofilm does. NO MODEL-SIDE IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS: structure.py has two_point_correlation and correlation_length, both SPATIAL, so running this against CPM output needs new code. represented_by_model is judged on this table's own terms — the CPM rearranges, so its dynamics do produce a temporal occupancy autocorrelation — and NOT on the strength of an existing function. Assumes stationarity: subtracting a per-voxel mean over a developing biofilm mixes growth, translation, interface motion and internal rearrangement into one number.
